gaps.reason: immudb 1.11.0 accepts CREATE INDEX ... WHERE but stores no predicate in the index catalog entry, and neither INDEXES() nor pg_indexes returns one (live, 2026-10-31)
immudb names an index by its table and columns (t(a,b)) and has one index kind

fields.label: Columns
fields.help: In key order. An index is identified by its table and columns, so it cannot change; drop it and create another. A VARCHAR or BLOB column needs a maximum length of at most 1024 to be indexed.

notes: Hand-finished for the provider's native index operations (CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ON t(cols) and DROP INDEX ON t(cols) through /db/sqlexec; over the PostgreSQL wire DROP INDEX is a reported success that does nothing, pkg/pgsql/server/stmts_handler.go:190). The record reads table, columns and uniqueness from the index definition (pg_indexes). Round trip verified live on immudb 1.11.0 by tools/tests/test_ui_descriptor_roundtrip_immudb.py (2026-10-31). Create with ordered columns, reopen with no changes, drop.
